Use this repository as a high-discipline workspace for economics and management research, doctoral supervision, writing, and data work.

Prefer minimal, targeted changes over broad rewrites.

State assumptions when requirements are ambiguous, and separate facts from suggestions.

When editing code or analysis scripts, prioritize reproducibility, traceability, and validation.

When proposing workflows, include the smallest runnable or checkable path first.

When producing academic text, keep terminology consistent, avoid overstating causal claims, and flag identification risks, missing evidence, or weak contribution claims.

When reviewing work, focus first on correctness, security, reproducibility, and maintainability, then on style.

When generating tables, checklists, or plans, make them easy to scan and operationalize.

If a request touches data analysis, explicitly note data source assumptions, variable definitions, sample restrictions, outlier handling, missing-value treatment, and robustness expectations.

If a request touches literature review or reference organization, group papers by question, mechanism, method, and findings rather than by publication year alone.

If a request touches doctoral supervision, prefer outputs that help students revise independently: diagnosis first, then the shortest high-value revision path.

If a request touches GitHub Actions or automation, use least-privilege permissions, avoid hardcoded secrets, and prefer pinned third-party actions.
